issues.legal_issue: The death sentence for murder was not justified where the crime arose from a dispute, the offender was not a habitual criminal, the circumstances were unlikely to recur, and the crime was not committed for personal gain.
material_facts: The appellant was convicted of murdering a young boy.
The murder arose from a land dispute involving the boy’s father and other persons.
The appellant was not a habitual criminal.
The circumstances leading to the crime were unlikely to recur.
The crime was not committed for personal gain.
The lower courts imposed the death sentence and gave special reasons for doing so.
issues.conclusion: The death sentence was set aside and life imprisonment was imposed instead.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 302 of the Indian Penal Code and 354(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the normal sentence for murder is life imprisonment, and the death sentence is reserved for very extreme and rare cases. The Court applied Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab, which requires the normal-sentence rule to be observed in letter and spirit.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_challenging_death_sentence_for_murder and dispute_triggered_the_crime and offender_not_habitual and triggering_circumstances_unlikely_to_recur and crime_not_for_personal_gain

predicates.criminal_appeal_challenging_death_senten: An accused appealed a death sentence imposed for murder.
predicates.dispute_triggered_the_crime: The crime arose from a dispute involving persons connected to the victim.
predicates.offender_not_habitual: The offender was not a habitual criminal.
predicates.triggering_circumstances_unlikely_to_rec: The circumstances that led to the crime were unlikely to recur.
predicates.crime_not_for_personal_gain: The offender did not commit the crime for personal gain.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a death sentence for murder and the crime arose from a dispute, the offender was not habitual, the triggering circumstances were unlikely to recur, and the crime was not for personal gain, the death sentence is replaced with life imprisonment.

issues.legal_issue: A sentence imposed for a very serious crime should not be reduced or commuted to a lesser custodial term without weighty reasons.
material_facts: The Court considered the possibility of the government reducing or commuting the appellant’s sentence.
The Court regarded the murder as a very serious crime.
The Court expressed its expectation that the government would not reduce or commute the sentence to less than fourteen years save for weighty reasons.
The Court’s observation was conditional on the validity of section 433A of the Code of Criminal Procedure being upheld; it did not decide that provision’s validity.
issues.conclusion: The Court expressed the expectation that the government would not reduce or commute the appellant’s sentence to less than fourteen years except for weighty reasons.
issues.legal_principle: The Court stated that, given the seriousness of the crime, the government should not reduce or commute the sentence below the stated period without weighty reasons. It framed this as an expectation, conditional on the validity of section 433A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, rather than deciding that provision’s validity.

predicates.criminal_appeal_concerning_murder_senten: An accused appealed in a criminal case concerning a sentence for murder.
predicates.sentence_imposed_for_very_serious_crime: The court regarded the crime for which the sentence was imposed as very serious.
predicates.executive_commutation_considered: The court addressed the possibility of the government reducing or commuting the sentence.

issues.definition: When a criminal appeal concerns a murder sentence for a very serious crime and executive commutation is considered, the government should not commute the sentence without weighty reasons.
